analysis.title: GS TMT TODAY 11.4.26
key_insights: Index futures rose off overnight highs (Nasdaq +40bps, S&P +90bps, Russell +140bps) after the midterm elections gave Democrats the majority in both the House and the Senate.
GS Econ expects Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to seek to limit the war with Iran, roll back selected tariffs and reverse spending cuts enacted last year.

GS Econ sees little federal change to data center and AI regulation, since new rules still need bipartisan Senate support and must overcome a veto. State and local Democratic wins are likely to bring short-term data center moratoria, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.
Election movers in TMT: hyperscalers higher versus neoclouds lower, SPCX/TSLA lower, power stocks lower.
AMD rose 1.5% after an initial +10% reaction on 4Q guidance that was better than feared after the INTC print, as datacenter and CPU growth offsets PC headwinds.

AMD 3Q revenue was $13.4bn vs GS $13.3bn and Street $13.1bn. Non-GAAP operating EPS was $2.09 vs GS $2.03 and Street $1.95. Datacenter revenue was $8.5bn (+97% y/y), above GS $8.26bn and Street $8.24bn.

AMD guided 4Q revenue to $17.0bn at the midpoint vs Street $16.3bn and GS $17.6bn. Datacenter is guided up about 50% q/q. Management expects CY27 Datacenter growth well over 100% y/y and company revenue growth over 80%.

ANET rose 6.5% (up as much as 18% overnight) on a big beat. 2026 guidance was raised (revenue +48% y/y at the midpoint) and the initial 2027 outlook is revenue growth of 38-40%, gross margin 62-64%, EBIT margin 49%, AI revenue doubling to $7bn and campus revenue of $2bn. GS raised its above-consensus 2027/28 EPS by about 10% to $6.13/$7.83.
ANET pushback areas flagged by GS are the q/q decline in deferred revenue and the deceleration in bookings growth.
DDOG fell 19% on a 3Q beat but 4Q guidance below elevated expectations. 4Q revenue was guided to $1.19-1.2bn (+25% y/y) vs consensus of $1.2bn. MDB, SNOW and NET fell in sympathy.

SMCI rose 5% after F1Q27 EPS of $1.81 (guidance $1.01-$1.10) on revenue of $19.9bn. FY27 revenue guidance was raised to $72-$82bn from $65-$72bn, constrained by component availability and data center readiness. Management does not expect to need additional capital.
UBER results and guidance were in line: Q3 gross bookings $59.82bn vs GSe $60.06bn, Q4 gross bookings guide $63.25-65.25bn vs Street $64.26bn, and Q4 EPS guide $0.95-0.99 vs Street $0.97.
BKNG had mixed results. Q3 gross bookings, room nights and adjusted EBITDA beat, but revenue missed and Q4 room nights were guided below. Management flagged Middle East and European disruptions.

DUOL rose 16% pre-market on a Q3 beat across bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA and a FY26 guidance raise. DAUs grew 29% y/y, accelerating from 23% in Q2. Q4 guidance implies modest gross margin pressure and roughly flat adjusted EBITDA y/y.
GS reinstated Skyworks (SWKS) at Sell with a 12-month target of $78, citing about 60% smartphone exposure that dampens growth despite benefits from the Qorvo combination.
Macro: Asia was mixed (Japan down nearly 1.5%, Hong Kong up over 1.5%, China up over 2%), European markets were up over 1%, Treasury yields were down about 4bp at the back end and WTI was down 0.9%.
Trump said he would accept the election results and is prepared to work with Democrats (Bloomberg).
Calendar: US Services PMI and EU flash inflation on 11/4, BoE rate decision on 11/5, and US NFP on 11/6 (prior +29k).

earnings_insights: AMD 3Q reported (11/3): revenue $13.4bn vs GS $13.3bn and Street $13.1bn. Non-GAAP operating EPS $2.09 vs GS $2.03 and Street $1.95. Gross margin 55.9% vs GS 56.2% and Street 56.1%.
AMD 4Q guidance (estimate by company): revenue $17.0bn at the midpoint vs Street $16.3bn and GS $17.6bn. Non-GAAP gross margin 55%. Implied non-GAAP EPS ex SBC $2.92 vs Street $2.65 and GS $2.97.
ANET 3Q26 reported: EPS, revenue and margin beat. 2026 guide raised to revenue +48% y/y at the midpoint. Initial 2027 outlook is revenue +38-40% y/y. GS 2027/28 EPS estimates are $6.13/$7.83.
DDOG 3Q reported: revenue $1.2bn (+35% y/y) vs guide $1.135-1.145bn, operating margin 28%. 4Q guide revenue $1.19-1.2bn (+25% y/y) vs consensus $1.2bn, operating margin about 23%.

UBER Q3 reported: gross bookings $59.82bn vs GSe $60.06bn and Street (FactSet) $59.83bn. Revenue $14.77bn vs GSe $14.58bn and Street $14.67bn. Adjusted EBITDA $2.96bn vs GSe $2.90bn. Non-GAAP EPS $0.88 vs GSe and Street $0.86. Q4 guide: gross bookings $63.25-65.25bn and non-GAAP EPS $0.95-0.99.

BKNG Q3 reported: gross bookings, room nights and adjusted EBITDA above GSe/Street and guidance. Revenue below estimates on product mix and booking timing. Q4 room nights guided below. Marketing expense +11% y/y. $650m of annual run-rate savings on track for 2027.
DUOL Q3 reported: bookings, revenue and adjusted EBITDA above GSe/Street and guidance. FY26 guidance raised on all three metrics. DAUs +29% y/y. Q4 adjusted EBITDA guided roughly flat y/y.

SMCI F1Q27 reported: EPS $1.81 vs guidance $1.01-$1.10. Revenue $19.9bn vs preannounced $18.5-$19.5bn and original guidance $14.5-$15.5bn. Gross margin 12.8%. FY27 revenue guide raised to $72-$82bn from $65-$72bn.

Earnings due 11/4 pre-market include DDOG, UBER, CRCL, CDW and NYT. After the close: APP, ARM, QCOM, COHR, SNAP, MELI, HUBS and others. 11/5 includes ABNB, NET, AFRM, AXON, LYFT, IONQ and MCHP after the close. VST and CHTR report 11/6 pre-market.
